reason: The graded material can become blocks for the protective shell.
expectation: The mold and furnace will produce wall blocks, though they may need assembly.

alternatives.reason: Insulating the water line also addresses a goal, but I want to start the wall first.

effect: The mold produced interlocking blocks, ready to build the shell.
reaction: The interlocking shape makes the construction feel practical.
reason: Place the blocks around the cabin to build the protective wall.
expectation: A freestanding wall will surround the cabin, perhaps with further work needed.

alternatives.reason: The line also needs shelter, but I want to finish placing the blocks first.

effect: The blocks form a freestanding wall, but the cabin protection goal remains unfinished.
reaction: I like that the wall stands separately from the pressure skin.
reason: The shovel may add soil around the wall and finish its protection.
expectation: Some material will be piled against or behind the wall; I am unsure exactly how.

alternatives.reason: The water line remains to be sheltered, but I am following the wall construction.

effect: The berm completes cabin protection, and the heater cycling off suggests less heat loss.
reaction: The window remaining open to the plain is a pleasing human detail; I would like a little more explanation of the berm's structure.
reason: Wrapping the connected line with the quilt is the remaining offered combination and addresses its shelter.
expectation: The water line will be insulated or wrapped, perhaps completing the remaining goal.

effect: The quilt insulates the line, but shelter still requires another action.
reaction: The extra step suggests insulation alone is not the full shelter.
reason: The shovel is the only offered combination and may bury the insulated line.
expectation: The line will be covered with soil for further protection, completing its goal.

effect: The shovel turns the insulated line into a service trench and completes the shelter goal.
reaction: The result is sensible, though I wanted a little more about how the trench protects the line.

mostWorthwhile.text: Berming the cabin made the result tangible: the heater cycles off and the window still shows the plain. It connects construction to daily life.

leastWorthwhile.text: The line steps were straightforward and ended with only an item name, so I learned little about the trench itself.

surprise.text: The detail that the window still looked out across the plain made the protected cabin feel inhabited.

arbitrary.text: Using the shovel on the wall made broad sense as berming, but I could not tell exactly where the material went or how the wall prevented loading the cabin.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: using local material to improve a lived-in station is appealing, though I would hope for more explanation and less straightforward assembly.
